title: System Evaluation Metrics

structured_notes.concern: The STUDENT needed guidance on how to present system evaluation data effectively and honestly for their final academic defense.
structured_notes.action_taken: The TEACHER explained how to contextualize the System Usability Scale (SUS) score and visually represent the data for the panel.
structured_notes.outcome: The STUDENT will calculate the final score, create bar charts, and transparently include negative feedback to support their future recommendations.
structured_notes.remarks: Honesty in system evaluation shows academic maturity and a deep understanding of software iteration. The STUDENT is ready to finalize the presentation slides.

reference_transcript:
Student: Sir, we are preparing for our final system presentation. How should we present our user testing results?
Teacher: You need clear, objective metrics. Do not just stand there and say "the users liked it." What evaluation tool did you use for the testing?
Student: We used the System Usability Scale (SUS) questionnaire for our 30 test users. We have all the raw scores in a spreadsheet.
Teacher: Good. Calculate the final average SUS score. If it is above 68, your system is considered usable by industry standards. Show a bar chart breaking down the scores.
Student: I will make a chart for the presentation. Should we mention the negative feedback too, or hide it?
Teacher: Absolutely mention it. Mentioning user struggles shows you did a real, honest evaluation. No system is perfect on the first version.
Student: Won't the panel subtract points if we admit the system has flaws?
Teacher: Not if you handle it correctly. Use the negative feedback to explain your future recommendations chapter. It shows you know how to iterate and improve the software.
Student: I see. I will prepare the charts and list the negative points as areas for future improvement. Thank you for all your help, Sir.
reference_summary: The STUDENT asked for advice on presenting final testing results. The TEACHER instructed them to use clear SUS metrics, visual charts, and to embrace negative feedback as a bridge to system recommendations. The STUDENT will update the presentation slides accordingly to ensure a strong defense.
